findings.title: Short termination notice period
findings.deviation: The draft allows for 14 days' notice for convenience, whereas the AtliQ playbook requires a minimum of 30 days for reasonable notice.
findings.impact: AtliQ risks losing the contractor on very short notice, potentially disrupting the Harrington project delivery.
findings.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason on fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other Party.
findings.counterPosition: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason on thirty (30) days' written notice to the other Party.

findings.title: Missing contractor indemnity
findings.deviation: The agreement contains no indemnity clause. AtliQ's playbook requires contractors to indemnify AtliQ for their own breach, negligence, and IP infringement.
findings.impact: AtliQ is fully exposed to Harrington's uncapped indemnity claims (which cover even Harrington's own negligence) without any contractual recourse against the contractor who actually performs the work.
findings.quote: (No indemnity clause present in Article 9 or elsewhere in the document)
findings.counterPosition: Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless AtliQ from and against all third-party claims and losses arising out of Contractor's negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of this Agreement, including any claim that the Work Product infringes third-party IP rights.
findings.linkedQuote: Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client... from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables... regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.

findings.title: Missing HIPAA/BAA flow-down
findings.deviation: The draft only provides for standard confidentiality (NDA) but does not include the Business Associate Agreement (BAA) required by the client for handling PHI.
findings.impact: AtliQ is in breach of the Harrington BAA, which mandates that all subcontractors handling PHI sign a back-to-back BAA with identical restrictions.
findings.quote: The Parties have entered into, or will enter into, a Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement, which shall also apply.
findings.counterPosition: The Contractor shall execute the AtliQ Sub-Business Associate Agreement prior to performing any Services involving Protected Health Information, and shall comply with all data security requirements set forth in the Client Contract.
findings.linkedQuote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor agrees in writing, prior to any access to PHI, to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.

findings.title: Missing domestic PHI restriction
findings.deviation: The agreement does not restrict the location of PHI access, whereas the client contract strictly forbids any access to PHI from outside the United States.
findings.impact: If the contractor accesses the client environment while traveling abroad, AtliQ would be in material breach of the Harrington BAA.
findings.quote: The Company shall provide the Contractor with user accounts and access credentials to the Company's project repositories and communication tools as needed for the Services.
findings.counterPosition: Contractor shall not, and shall ensure that its personnel do not, access, store, or process any Client PHI from any location outside the United States.
findings.linkedQuote: No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States without Client's prior written consent.

findings.title: IP assignment timing gap
findings.deviation: Contractor IP assignment is 'effective upon payment', whereas the Harrington contract requires AtliQ to own deliverables 'from creation'.
findings.impact: There is a legal gap where AtliQ might deliver work to Harrington that it does not yet technically own, potentially causing a breach of the client's ownership warranty.
findings.quote: the Contractor hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in it... effective upon payment for the Services to which it relates.
findings.counterPosition: Contractor hereby assigns all right, title and interest in the Work Product to the Company immediately upon creation.
findings.linkedQuote: All Deliverables... shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.

findings.title: Missing mandatory background checks
findings.deviation: The agreement fails to require the background checks, drug screenings, and compliance training mandated by the Harrington contract for all personnel.
findings.impact: AtliQ cannot permit the contractor to access Harrington's systems without these checks, likely delaying the project start.
findings.quote: The Contractor shall perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and shall comply with the Company's reasonable instructions regarding deliverables and timelines.
findings.counterPosition: Contractor shall complete and pass all background checks, drug screenings, and compliance training required by the Client as a condition of performing the Services.
findings.linkedQuote: Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.

fine.note: The 1x fees cap is mutual and includes standard carve-outs for fraud and confidentiality.
The non-solicitation clause is mutual, limited to 6 months, and does not include a non-compete, which is fair for a freelancer.
